name: islamhouse
method: official public API (free key published in the site's own docs)
license: Not explicitly stated for content reuse/ML -- only a visitor-data privacy policy was found, not a content license -- marked needs_approval per your instruction to keep unclear-license sources out of train
notes: REACHABLE (200 OK). Found a real, documented public API (api.islamhouse.com redirects to https://developers.islamhouse.com, whose Postman collection at https://documenter.gw.postman.com/api/collections/7929737/TzkyMfPc lists 37 endpoints under base https://api3.islamhouse.com/v3/paV29H2gm56kvLPy/..., free public API key confirmed working live: main/get-available-languages, main/get-item/<id>/<lang>/json, main/get-item-translations/<id>/<lang>/json (returns sibling item ids in every other available language for the same work -- true cross-language alignment), quran/* endpoints, etc). BOOKS: confirmed PDF-only (no inline text field) via main/get-item/2839210/ar/json and a book detail page (islamhouse.com/en/books/1261/, two .pdf links). ARTICLES (checked this pass, type slug confirmed = 'articles' plural, found via main/get-category-types-available/<catId>/ar/ar/json's api_url): DOES have a real full_description HTML field, unlike books -- but it's unreliable, not a clean win. A 200-item probe of Arabic articles spread across the full 2007-2026 time range (main/get-latest/all/articles/ar/ar/<page>/10/json, pages 1..161 step 8) found: 79/200 (39.5%) have substantial inline text (full_description >200 chars) -- but only 3/200, 2/200, 7/200, 2/200, 0/200 (en/fr/id/ur/tr respectively) even HAVE a translation into our 5 target languages via main/get-item-translations, and of those few, only about half also have inline text on the target-language side too (e.g. en: 1/3 had text on both sides; fr: 0/2; id: 1/7; ur: 0/2; tr: 0/0 found at all). Per-language translated-article COUNTS reported by the API are larger (en 494, fr 229, id 820, ur 156, tr 284 of 1,672 total) but this sample suggests the actual (inline-text-on-both-sides) fraction of those is small and would require probing every candidate individually with no way to predict the yield in advance. CONCLUSION: not the same as books (some articles genuinely have text), but the practical yield for building an ar<->{en,fr,id,ur,tr} sentence pair source is negligible and unpredictable without an expensive full-corpus probe, and NO content-reuse/ML terms were found beyond the visitor-data-only privacy policy at d1.islamhouse.com/html/policy.htm regardless. Per your instruction (mark needs_approval and keep out of train when ML-use terms are unclear), NOT scraped in bulk and no downloader was written -- decision treated the same as books despite the partial inline-text exception.
